record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: Substantially extend the theory of interconnections of infinite-dimensional integral-input-to-state-stable systems, whose current state is much less complete than the corresponding ISS interconnection theory. This includes sharper small-gain results and a more systematic coupling theory for iISS subsystems.

evidence.quote: • Theory of couplings of infinite-dimensional iISS systems is far less complete than in the ISS case (see [92] for a survey of such results in ODE case).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider control systems on Banach spaces of the form
  ẋ = A x + f(x, u),
where A generates a strongly continuous semigroup on a Banach space X, u is an input from a function space U, and the resulting evolution is well-posed.

Such a system is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist a class-KL function β and class-K functions α, γ such that for every initial state x₀ ∈ X and every admissible input u, the solution x(·) satisfies
  α(‖x(t)‖_X) ≤ β(‖x₀‖_X, t) + ∫₀ᵗ γ(‖u(s)‖_U) ds   for all t ≥ 0.

Now consider a feedback interconnection of two (or finitely many) such infinite-dimensional iISS subsystems
  ẋ_i = A_i x_i + f_i(x_1, …, x_n, u),   i = 1, …, n,
in which the "inputs" of subsystem i include the states x_j of the other subsystems plus an external input u.

Develop a substantial theory for such interconnections of infinite-dimensional iISS systems. In particular:

(a) Formulate sharp small-gain conditions on the iISS gain functions γ_{ij} (governing the influence of x_j on x_i) that guarantee iISS of the overall interconnected system on the product space X_1 × … × X_n.

(b) Provide a systematic coupling theory for infinite-dimensional iISS subsystems, including Lyapunov-based and trajectory-based criteria, that parallels and substantially extends the existing interconnection theory available for finite-dimensional iISS systems and for infinite-dimensional ISS systems.

The task is to establish such small-gain theorems and coupling criteria with the same level of completeness already achieved for ISS interconnections in the infinite-dimensional setting.
artifact.status_search_result: Several partial results exist: iISS small-gain theorems for two interconnected distributed-parameter systems and constructions of iISS Lyapunov functions for interconnected parabolic PDEs have been established, and recent works extend ISS small-gain theorems to infinite networks of heterogeneous infinite-dimensional systems. However, a complete and systematic coupling theory for infinite-dimensional iISS systems comparable to the ISS case is not yet available, so the broader program remains open.

status_evidence.title: Construction of iISS Lyapunov functions for interconnected parabolic systems
status_evidence.snippet: Methods to construct Lyapunov functions characterizing iISS of interconnected infinite-dimensional parabolic systems.
status_evidence.claim: Partial iISS interconnection results exist for parabolic PDE systems via Lyapunov constructions.

status_evidence.title: Small gain theorems for general networks of heterogeneous infinite-dimensional systems
status_evidence.snippet: A small-gain theorem applies to interconnections of nonlinear heterogeneous ISS control systems covering PDE, delay and ODE systems.
status_evidence.claim: Substantial progress on ISS interconnections of infinite-dimensional systems, but the iISS analog is less developed.

status_evidence.title: Nonlinear small-gain theorems for input-to-state stability of infinite interconnections
status_evidence.snippet: Extends nonlinear small-gain theorems for ISS from finite to countably infinite networks.
status_evidence.claim: Recent advances target ISS rather than iISS interconnections in the infinite-dimensional setting.
